limitations: Derived statistics only; no benchmark, test, install, browser, server or product operation was rerun.
CPU frequency/affinity, background CPU load, GC and OS caches were not controlled. These are separate observational cohorts, not a controlled performance experiment.
No SLO, statistical significance, causal attribution, speedup or faster/slower product conclusion is asserted.
All finite recorded metric values are included, regardless of sample status; missing/non-finite values and failed attempts are counted explicitly.
Measured samples and warmups are never pooled. Cold aggregate rows summarize the same six existing single-process samples, not additional attempts.
PerCommandMs is the per-sample batch total divided by 24/96/384 history frames; its median is not the median of individual command latency observations.
Corpus recipe, sizes and fixture structure are identical; independently generated document/entity IDs make actual serialized corpus hashes different.
Solve uses warm direct PlaneGCS and bypasses the browser LRU; cache-hit timing and browser cold-start were NOT_RUN.
Fresh Node WASM initialization is not OS disk-cache cold. MemoryCadProjectHost timings do not measure browser/disk/network persistence.
Source products and dependency lock changed. Matching Node/native assets/tool definitions do not justify attributing any timing difference to one repair.
Original acceptedBaseline/status fields are preserved; deriving/comparing data does not grant technical or product acceptance.
Diagnostic bootstrap timings and raw per-operation arrays remain in source reports; they are not added to the original 53 repeated case-metric rows.
